items.article_search_text: Oscar Piastri led Formula One by a healthy margin this time last year but now, with his title dreams effectively over for another season, the Australian says he is doing all he can to give himself the best shot at a championship challenge in 2027. That means winning at least… Oscar Piastri led Formula One by a healthy margin this time last year but now, with his title dreams effectively over for another season, the Australian says he is doing ... Oscar Piastri led Formula One by a healthy margin this time last year but now, with his title dreams effectively over for another season, the Australian says he is doing all he can to give himself the best shot at a championship challenge in 2027. That means winning at least one race to help rescue a disappointing year after the highs of 2025 and, with leaders Mercedes disappearing over the horizon, helping champions McLaren beat Ferrari to second place in the constructors’ standings. The 25-year-old was 31 points clear of British teammate Lando Norris, the eventual champion, at the top after the September 7 Italian Grand Prix last year and had won seven of 16 races. Piastri left Monza this year still without a win to his credit after 13 rounds and 151 points behind Mercedes’ championship leader Kimi Antonelli but fifth in that race and feeling he had taken “a much better step in the right direction. “Of course, I would love to win a race or two this year, or more if I can,” he told Reuters at the Spanish Grand Prix. “But for me, honestly, the biggest thing, the end goal is to try and win championships. And if I can’t do that this year, then I want to make sure I’m as best prepared as I can for next year.” REASONABLE CHANCE OF BEATING FERRARI Piastri’s best result in the first season of the sport’s new engine and rules era has been second place behind Antonelli in Japan last March, while teammate Lando Norris has won twice. The Australian started the season with two ‘did not starts’, including one at home in Melbourne. “Never say never but it is going to be incredibly challenging for the championship,” said the Australian with typical deadpan understatement. “(We’re) trying to do the best we can in the constructors’ championship because, whilst I think beating Mercedes is going to be tricky, I think we do have a reasonable chance of trying to beat Ferrari. Just trying to win races if we can and learn as much as we can for next year.” Ferrari are currently second, 59 points ahead of McLaren. Mercedes are 122 further in front. Piastri’s 2025 season nose-dived from a point where he seemed destined to take the title to being overtaken by Norris and then Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, ending up third overall. His most recent win was the Dutch Grand Prix in August last year. The Australian denied that the knock-on effects of that campaign, and the mental toll of coming to terms with the crown slipping through his hands in what might even have been the opportunity of a lifetime, had seeped over into 2026. “It’s all to do with technically driving the car. There’s nothing to do with a hangover from last year … it’s very much a technical thing,” he said. “It’s not like I’m slow, feeling sorry for myself or thinking about last year. It’s just that a few of the weekends I’ve had to drive the car in a different way that just hasn’t really worked for me. “The biggest thing this year has been the cars are very different to drive, both from a power unit point of view but also the car itself is fundamentally very different and the tyres also. There’s just been a lot of challenges around that and how you extract performance out of the car. “You’ve got to drive it very differently and I would say it’s not necessarily in the way that I would choose to drive a race car. So there’s just been some struggles getting to grips with that.”

items.article_search_text: Andrea Stella defends the philosophy of letting his drivers compete, but admits that the internal battle cost them time against Verstappen. The team will review the clash to see if they could have managed it better and optimized the final result. The Italian Grand Prix left a new chapter in the relationship between the McLaren [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/mclaren]drivers. Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri had a tense duel in the final stages of the race that ended with the Briton putting two wheels on the grass and accusing his teammate of having pushed him off track. After this episode, Andrea Stella, the team principal, has assured that McLaren will review the incident to determine if they could have managed the situation better. The altercation occurred in the final laps of the race, when both drivers were fighting for fourth position. Norris overtook Piastri on lap 48 but the Australian recovered the position one lap later. The Briton tried to return the overtake but found a gap that was closing and ended up with two wheels on the grass, suggesting that Piastri "pushed me off." The tension was evident on the team radio. Stella, however, downplayed the incident: "When we reviewed it I think we saw that the episode is much more benign than it might have seemed in the heat of the moment" declared the Italian. The McLaren boss explained that the decision not to interfere in the fight between his drivers was intentional: "The two cars were on the same tires, the same tire age, the same car, so we thought there was no need to interfere in the normal development of the race. We let them compete, we believe it was the right thing to do" he stated. F1 Daily: Antonelli's Monza Miracle, Hamilton's Frustration, and Audi's Protest [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/0e98c448-e7bd-4879-939b-9f6f37e9f416.jpeg] F1 Daily: Antonelli's Monza Miracle, Hamilton's Frustration, and Audi's Protest Alpine's Pierre Gasly delivered one of the best, most surprisingly good qualifying performances this season. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/f1-daily-antonellis-monza-miracle-hamiltons-frustration-and-audis-protest] The team has a history of internal reviews after the Monza race. Last year, McLaren's famous "papaya rules" were under the spotlight when Piastri was ordered to let Norris pass. On this occasion, the analysis will focus on whether the internal battle cost them a better position against their rivals: "I think you're right to highlight that as soon as you fight with your teammate, you can lose time. So, was there a better way for McLaren to face Max Verstappen? We will review it" admitted Stella. The Dutchman from Red Bull was the big beneficiary of the duel between the McLarens. Verstappen managed to overtake both to take the third step of the podium behind the Mercedes of George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. Stella acknowledged the superiority of the Red Bull: "I think overall Max was faster, he just got caught in that hook you have this year when you lose the tow here at Monza and you have to use energy to defend yourself from someone else" he explained. Norris and His Salary Gap With Hamilton and Verstappen [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/3392ea03-9ac6-49b7-9c78-3fcd2fa90ff7.jpeg] Norris and His Salary Gap With Hamilton and Verstappen The world champion acknowledged that he had a raise after renewing, but denied astronomical figures. He states that his rivals' track records justify their million dollar contracts, although he trusts he can match them in the future with his on track performance. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/norris-and-his-salary-gap-with-hamilton-and-verstappen] The review of the incident will be an exercise in self criticism for McLaren. The team seeks to optimize its performance and prevent internal competition from costing them options in the championship. Stella trusts that the analysis will allow them to find areas of improvement in the management of duels between their drivers without giving up the philosophy of letting them compete. The constructors' championship is very tight and every point is vital. McLaren knows it cannot afford to lose opportunities due to a lack of coordination between its drivers. The review of the Monza duel will be key to establishing clearer guidelines for the future and ensuring that the ambition of Norris and Piastri translates into the best possible result for the team.

items.article_search_text: More teams are dissecting their performance at Monza, especially with the Spanish Grand Prix coming up. It has been a couple of days since Kimi Antonelli won [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/race-day/antonelli-makes-history-at-monza-and-wins-from-the-back] the 2026 Italian Grand Prix. And yet, teams around the F1 paddock are still analyzing what went wrong (and right) for them at the Temple of Speed. It's not a surprise, though. We had so much going on during the Italian GP that it's perfectly reasonable to talk about it days after. MCLAREN EXPLAINS HECTIC MONZA WEEKEND After a disappointing performance in the qualifying sessions, McLaren gave their fans a better show on Sunday. Reigning World Champion Lando Norris finished fourth, just a spot ahead of teammate Oscar Piastri. But the McLaren garage had a huge scare when Norris and Piastri came to blows in the latter stages of the race. Norris found himself on the grass at the exit of Curva Grande, but he still managed to come back and overtake Piastri in the final lap. McLaren team principal Andrea Stella had nothing negative to say about the battle between his two drivers. Instead, he applauded his team's resiliency in bouncing back from a difficult Saturday to a more productive Sunday. HADJAR OFFICIALLY SITS OUT AT MADRID As expected, Red Bull Racing has confirmed that Isack Hadjar will miss his third straight race [https://www.espn.ph/f1/story/_/id/49860811/isack-hadjar-miss-f1-spanish-gp-liam-lawson-continues-red-bull] weekend. Liam Lawson will continue to drive for Red Bull's main team at the Spanish Grand Prix, while reserve driver Yuki Tsunoda stays on with the Racing Bulls. Lawson is coming off a difficult Monza race, where he lost important time due to front-wing damage. Meanwhile, Tsunoda, who was just in his second race this season, came through with his first points in 2026 [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/2026-italian-grand-prix-surprises-and-busts-at-the-temple-of-speed]. RED BULL HAVING FUN AT THEIR ADUO DEMISE Instead of sulking in the corner, the Red Bull social team is having fun referencing their Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) ranking. Here's one of their tweets [https://x.com/redbullracing/status/2096977540808364109], if you need a bit of a laugh to start your day. Red Bull-Ford Powertrains, in their first year as the team's engine manufacturer, was found to have the best Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) in the F1 grid. It's a good testament to their work, but under the ADUO rules, it also left them without an additional opportunity to upgrade their engine. MEKIES REFLECTS ON RED BULL'S PODIUM FINISH Despite Max Verstappen's complaints about their straight-line speed, Red Bull still gained some ground with a P3 finish. They were able to stay ahead of the likes of McLaren and Ferrari, two teams that were expected to strongly contend for the podium places at Monza. Mekies said that they're in the "right direction," but they won't be satisfied until they find the "ultimate speed" they're looking for. Let's see if Verstappen and Liam Lawson can extract more pace at the Madring.

items.article_search_text: Pierre Gasly had taken a shock pole but slipped to seventh. For McLaren, starting mid-pack at Monza meant every pass cost time and energy. McLaren recovered from a sloppy qualifying at Monza to finish fourth and fifth in the Italian Grand Prix, but the bigger story was what the pit wall chose not to do. With Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri on the same tyres and the same car, team principal Andrea Stella left them free to race rather than impose an order in the closing laps.Norris started eighth and finished fourth. Piastri started sixth and took fifth, 0.137 seconds behind. Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli won from 19th, George Russell was second and Max Verstappen held third. McLaren scored 22 points and left Italy arguing that execution, not team orders, decided the afternoon.Better race after a messy SaturdayOn Saturday, team principal Andrea Stella blamed poor execution for a Q3 that left Piastri sixth and Norris eighth. Piastri had been third before a three-place grid drop for impeding Liam Lawson. The MCL40 was also weak on Monza’s long straights.Sunday was cleaner. The pair moved forward in a race packed with slipstream fights and battery management.“I think this is a race in which we executed racing better than what we did yesterday,” Stella said. “Yesterday in Qualifying we should have qualified certainly better than a P6/P8 on the grid. And we reviewed that with the team and with the drivers, and we said to ourselves that today, from an execution point of view, we should have done better and operated higher standards.”Pierre Gasly had taken a shock pole but slipped to seventh. For McLaren, starting mid-pack at Monza meant every pass cost time and energy.Why the pit wall stayed quietLate in the race, Lando Norris wanted a run at Max Verstappen. The team decided he had to earn it on track.“I think in this situation, we thought that for Lando to be able to have a chance on Max, he should firstly be able to pass Oscar,” Stella said. “And the two cars were on the same tyres, same tyre age, same car. So we thought there was no need to interfere with the normal development of the race. We let them race.”“We think that was the right thing to do. I think overall Max was faster, he was just caught in this loop that you have when you lose the slipstream here in Monza, and you have to use the energy to defend from someone else.”Norris made the move stick on the final lap with a late power-unit boost. Piastri stayed right with him to the flag.The grass moment McLaren will reviewOn lap 51, Norris put two wheels on the grass at Curva Grande and radioed that Piastri had pushed him off. After the race, he accepted the defence was fair. Stella agreed.“The moment in which Lando put the wheels on the grass, he came on the radio, he made a comment like he pushed me off or something. But actually, when we reviewed it, I think we saw that the episode is much more benign than what it might have looked in the heat of the moment.”“So I think it's something that certainly we will review, and we will review in the context of this kind of racing. As soon as you fight with each other, then you may lose time. So was there a better way for McLaren to give a fight to Verstappen? We will review. It wasn't obvious to us on the pit wall, and we thought that it was more important to let them race according to our philosophy of going racing.”Oscar Piastri’s form, and where the MCL40 can win againStella also saw a step from Oscar Piastri after a few awkward races in this year’s car.“I think it's a race that confirms a trajectory with Oscar,” he said. “We've had a couple of races in which we saw that for the requirements of this year's car, especially in the race when the car slides, we needed to make some adaptations to his natural driving style.”The next stop is Madrid. Stella does not expect Monza-style drag to decide that race, and he is not getting carried away by the table. “I think our tracks will be more the likes of Malaysia, Austin, Brazil,” he said. “In Zandvoort and Hungary we were in position to win races, and here, while we were not, we know that it's a special race. Drag will be less important in Madrid. But from a championship point of view, I think we have to remain very realistic,don't get conditioned by looking at the classification, just focus on one race at a time.”

That was very dangerous," said Lando Norris, McLaren driver. "He moved back at me after I went to the inside."Piastri was instructed by his race engineer Tom Stallard to keep the racing clean, and Norris ultimately secured fourth place on the final lap, crossing the line two-tenths of a second ahead of his teammate.Speaking to accredited media including PlanetF1.com after the race, Norris retreated from his initial reaction on the team radio regarding Piastri's defensive driving."No, it was okay," said Lando Norris, McLaren driver. "I just need to review things, but it’s just the perception of when you’re in the car, when someone’s opening the gap a bit and then goes straight. You get that perception when you’re going at 200 miles per hour.So that’s all. I think what he did was fair. It’s just when you’re in the moment, and you’re half on the grass, you don’t realise how quickly things can end pretty badly.Just in the heat of the moment, but it was fine, and it was a good battle. A good result from a tough race."Addressing the team's underlying pace, Norris pointed out that the circuit exposed specific performance limitations relative to their rivals."I think so," said Lando Norris, McLaren driver. "I think we’ve seen in the past races, like Red Bull Ring, that the Red Bull can be very fast in those type of circuits with good top speeds and stuff, and that was again proven today. And they were better than us.But it was clear that the Mercedes are still in a league of their own compared to us. So you know, we won by bigger margins over the last few races, which they were still fighting for good points at those times, and we were not even close to fighting for our top two today. So just frustrating.But we said it before the weekend, and I think we’ve seen what our expectation was, and we still have work to do, which we knew. So yeah, it’s nothing that’s a surprise. We just need to really work on kind of the slower, medium-speed corners, the stability of the car, which is just not good enough, and some straight-line speed.If we can sort that, then yeah, a lot of stuff is sorted."In official team statements released after the race, Norris expressed satisfaction with his individual execution despite performance deficits."I'm happy with the race, finishing fourth was a good result for us today," said Lando Norris, McLaren driver. "The race was tough, the car was tricky, and I felt I drove well to maximise what we had. The second half was very strong, using the slipstream brought me back into the fight, and the battles with Lewis [Hamilton] and Oscar on the last lap were enjoyable.It was good, hard racing, and to come out ahead was satisfying. Despite the result, it's clear we're not where we need to be. This weekend highlighted our weaknesses - we're lacking in general performance, especially in Qualifying, and our straight-line speed is a disadvantage.Even with recent wins, we still have a lot of work to do as a team. We know our strengths and weaknesses, and the challenge now is to improve for the rest of the year."In post-race broadcast interviews reported by news.com.au, Norris reiterated that he held no ill will toward his teammate following the close call."It’s something I have to go and see," said Lando Norris, McLaren driver. "I don’t think so, honestly. It’s just when you’re in the car, things happen very quickly.And obviously, I kind of went to the left and he started to come back to the right, and then straightened up. So, sometimes, you get a feeling of something, but I don’t think he did anything wrong. So no, it was just a good, tough fight.Good racing from both of us, and enjoyable to come out with a P4 for me was a good day today, so I’m satisfied."Piastri highlighted his late-race strategy regarding battery management as the deciding factor in the battle."It was a good battle," said Oscar Piastri, McLaren driver. "A lot of back and forth. The last lap, you never really know what to do with the energy, and I think we went for different strategies with that, and he got past.I thought I’d have a chance to get back past again, but ultimately I just didn’t quite get there. So yeah, it was always a bit of a gamble with these cars, but yeah, I definitely know for next time what I would do different."Piastri also noted that the overall result reflected the maximum performance available from the MCL40 package at Monza."A tough battle for sure," said Oscar Piastri, McLaren driver. "We both seemed pretty even, especially at the end. It was challenging to know when to use your battery.We saw a good battle, I think it was good racing. I think it was the best result we could’ve got as a team, I’m happy."In the team's official media release, Piastri added that his recent personal form showed encouragement despite losing fourth place."I think this weekend was definitely the strongest I've felt for a while, and my pace was the most encouraging it has been in some time," said Oscar Piastri, McLaren driver. "It was a tough battle out there for sure. The racing was quite tricky with the back-and-forth effect, especially with Lewis [Hamilton] and then Max [Verstappen], which made it difficult to break away.You had to be quite smart in how you played it to avoid losing time. Ultimately, we were the third-quickest team today. Mercedes were clearly a lot quicker than everybody, and even Max had more pace than we anticipated.It was a good result for the team and probably the best result we could have got. It was an intense, hot race, but it's felt much better and hopefully, we can continue this positive momentum going forward."McLaren team principal Andrea Stella explained to media including Formula1.com and RacingNews365 why pit wall management chose not to intervene between the drivers during the race."I think this is a race in which we executed racing better than what we did yesterday," said Andrea Stella, McLaren Team Principal. "Yesterday in Qualifying we should have qualified certainly better than a P6/P8 on the grid. And we reviewed that with the team and with the drivers, and we said to ourselves that today, from an execution point of view, we should have done better and operated higher standards.I think overall, we did. We paid a bit of price of the position on the grid... it is not easy to get an overtake completed and move on – like if we see how much it took for Lando to pass [Pierre] Gasly, and then start to close the gap to the cars ahead. We see that there's certainly been quite a lot of entertainment today, but to some extent there were also some issues for a quicker car to be able to compete, if you don't start at the front of the grid.Very, very busy [for] everyone, drivers and engineers, with managing the power unit and the battery in a circuit like Monza."Stella reinforced that McLaren's policy allowed the drivers equal opportunity on matching tire strategies."I think in this situation, we thought that for Lando to be able to have a chance on Max, he should firstly be able to pass Oscar," said Andrea Stella, McLaren Team Principal. "And the two cars were on the same tyres, same tyre age, same car. So we thought there was no need to interfere with the normal development of the race.We let them race. We think that was the right thing to do. I think overall Max was faster, he was just caught in this loop that you have when you lose the slipstream here in Monza, and you have to use the energy to defend from someone else."Addressing Norris's grass excursion, Stella confirmed that video review lowered concerns over any potential violation."The moment in which Lando put the wheels on the grass, he came on the radio, he made a comment like he pushed me off or something," said Andrea Stella, McLaren Team Principal. "But actually, when we reviewed it, I think we saw that the episode is much more benign than what it might have looked in the heat of the moment. So I think it's something that certainly we will review, and we will review in the context of this kind of racing.As soon as you fight with each other, then you may lose time. So was there a better way for McLaren to give a fight to Verstappen? We will review.It wasn't obvious to us on the pit wall, and we thought that it was more important to let them race according to our philosophy of going racing."Stella expressed confidence in Piastri's adapted driving technique, pointing to recent race setups."I think it's a race that confirms a trajectory with Oscar," said Andrea Stella, McLaren Team Principal. "We've had a couple of races in which we saw that for the requirements of this year's car, especially in the race when the car slides, we needed to make some adaptations to his natural driving style. We kind of adopted the same approach that we used with Lando last year, and we saw pretty rapidly some developments.We were happy to see how competitive Oscar was in Zandvoort in Qualifying trim. We said we need to do a little bit more for the race trim, we put in some work. And it's good that this work seems like it's been useful here in Monza."Looking ahead to upcoming events in Madrid, Baku, and beyond, Stella outlined where the MCL40 will likely perform best."I think our tracks will be more the likes of Malaysia, Austin, Brazil," said Andrea Stella, McLaren Team Principal. "I think where we have some long corners, the car seems to express its potential well. We have some new upgrades that we will take to Baku, but we still think that tracks like Baku and Madrid, where you have to be very precise with the trajectory, short corners, maybe they don't play to the best of our car.In Zandvoort and Hungary we were in position to win races, and here, while we were not, we know that it's a special race. Drag will be less important in Madrid. But from a championship point of view, I think we have to remain very realistic – don't get conditioned by looking at the classification, just focus on one race at a time."In McLaren's official post-race summary, Stella extended congratulations to the race winners while evaluating the team's operational execution."First of all, congratulations to Andrea Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes on their victory today, they did a very good job and fully deserved the result," said Andrea Stella, McLaren Team Principal. "Overall, it was a positive and strong weekend for the team. The race was incredibly tense and entertaining, and both Lando and Oscar showed the same high level of performance throughout.What we saw today was good, hard racing that delivered an exciting spectacle for the fans. items.article_search_text: Lewis Hamilton gives damning verdict on F1 title hopes after Monza disappointment - latest: Follow live F1 updates from the Autodromo Nazionale Monza as Antonelli wins an incredible race with Russell missing out on victory Lewis Hamilton believes he can no longer catch Kimi Antonelli in the F1 world championship race after a day of disappointment at the Italian Grand Prix. Hamilton had high hopes of a strong showing at Ferrari’s home race but dropped down the order from fourth on lap one after a tangle with his teammate Charles Leclerc, who then crashed out a lap later. The Briton recovered to fourth but was then short of pace after his team opted not to pit him during a mid-race VSC [virtual safety car] period and ultimately finished sixth – behind both McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli claimed a sensational victory from 19th on the grid to extend his mighty lead in the standings. Hamilton now trails the 20-year-old Italian by 76 points with 10 rounds remaining. Ralf Schumacher paid a glowing tribute to his brother Michael on an Italian Grand Prix weekend where Ferrari are honouring their most successful Formula 1 driver. This season represents 30 years since Michael, six-and-a-half years older than fellow F1 driver and brother Ralf, made his debut for the Scuderia, a team he went on to win five consecutive world championships with. Both Lewis Hamilton's and Charles Leclerc’s cars will adorn Schumacher’s logo and seven stars on the chassis to represent Schumacher’s title tally – a feat only matched by Hamilton. On Sunday, Sebastian Vettel will also drive a “celebratory” lap in Schumacher’s title-winning 2002 car. Full story below: George Russell was booed by the Italian fans as home hero Kimi Antonelli claimed an improbable victory at Monza on Sunday. Antonelli became the first Italian winner at Monza in 60 years with a sensational drive from 19th on the grid to first at the chequered flag. The 20-year-old, on fresher tyres, overtook Russell in the closing stages to claim his seventh win of the season and extend his lead in the world championship to 66 points over his Mercedes teammate. “First of all, happy to see Charles unharmed after such a big accident. On our side, we executed a good race today and a strong weekend overall given our limitations. We put together a solid qualifying yesterday and had a good start and race pace today. “Boxing under the VSC got us ahead of Ocon with a great pit stop from our mechanics and good pace allowed us to overtake Bearman at the end. I'm now very much looking forward to Madrid next weekend.” “We knew that this race would be challenging, especially in terms of our top speed, and that made it difficult for Lewis to fight and overtake the cars around him. Regarding Charles, on the second lap he was side by side with Oscar (Piastri) going into the last corner and went slightly onto the dirty side of the track, which was enough for him to lose the car and hit the barriers. It was a big impact, so the most important thing is that Charles is okay. “Of course, we are disappointed that we could not give our tifosi the result we wanted after the incredible energy and support they have shown us throughout the weekend. I’m very happy for Kimi (Antonelli): this is a very important moment for him, and he deserves it. Our focus now immediately switches to next weekend and the new Madrid circuit.” Kimi Antonelli dealt a seismic blow to George Russell’s hopes of taking the F1 world championship by passing his Mercedes teammate with just three laps remaining to win the Italian Grand Prix after he started 19th on the grid. Home favourite Antonelli, who was way down the order after a grid penalty, took advantage of a favourable strategy, an explosive new engine and a demonstration of passing excellence, to become the first Italian in 60 years to win in Monza. Full report below: Should you have pitted? “One of the harder ones to swallow today, was hoping for more. But yeah... I gave it absolutely everything, just didn’t have the speeds on the straights, was a sitting duck. “We’ll look internally into what we could have done better, we probably should have been on the hard tyre but we also had to be overtaking people. I thought they’d stop us, they didn’t, and I ran out of tyres.” On prioritisation in team: “Yeah, too far past that already. Too late for that now. I lost a lot of points today; they’re just ahead. We’ll do our best to keep pushing the rest of the seaosn, they’re out ahead now.” “Went on power, didn’t feel like the car was quite alright, lost the car, need to look at the data. “For the start, not much to say, Lewis tried to overtake, there wasn’t much space, kept it tight into turn two.” “I woke up this morning and I felt very good mentally, I thought a good result would’ve been podium, after the red flag I was already P12, then top-five and I knew I had a shot for the win. It was difficult to break away, we managed to pull it off and bring it home. Championship, yours to lose? “No not at all, race by race, you never know what can happen, today went well, we had a massive opportunity and we took it. Madrid is a new challenge, new track for everyone, important to be on point. Will enjoy this moment then focus on the next one.” “Some good battles out there, had to send it around the outside a lot. In general, top speed wasn’t our friend today. Tried to hang in there, they were a bit too fast, tried to be in overtake mode. Tried to do my own race. “I had one tricky moment in turn 2 and the tarmac was opening up. Makes quite a big difference around here; happy with P3.”

items.article_search_text: Home driver Kimi Antonelli has claimed a stunning win at the F1 Italian Grand Prix after Charles Leclerc... Championship leader Kimi Antonelli dealt a seismic blow to rival George Russell's title hopes by passing his Mercedes teammate with just three laps remaining to win the Italian Grand Prix. Home favourite Antonelli, who was way down the order after a grid penalty, took advantage of a favourable strategy, an explosive new engine and a demonstration of passing excellence on Sunday, to become the first Italian in 60 years to win in Monza. Charles Leclerc was earlier forced out of race after a 160-mph horror crash on lap two in what was a nightmare start for Ferrari in their home race. Leclerc lost control of his car on the exit of the high-speed Curva Parabolica as he duelled with Australia's Oscar Piastri for fourth position. The Monegasque flew through the gravel trap at the exit of the final corner before thudding into the tyre barrier and sustaining significant damage to his car at the end of the second lap. McLaren driver Piastri was not affected by the incident and the 25-year-old Melburnian was able to continue after the re-start to eventually finish in fifth place. "I think this weekend was definitely the strongest I've felt for a while, and my pace was the most encouraging it has been in some time," Piastri said. "It was a good result for the team and probably the best result we could have got." Antonelli crossed the line 3.8 seconds clear of Briton Russell to extend his lead from 59 points to 66 and follow in Ferrari's Ludovico Scarfiotti's footsteps as the first Italian to win at Monza's Temple of Speed since 1966. "Oh my god ... it feels like a dream," Antonelli said after banking his seventh win of the season. "It's unbelievable. I never would have believed I would be here today, but I am so happy." Red Bull's Max Verstappen finished third, one place ahead of world champion Lando Norris. Norris' fellow Brition, Lewis Hamilton, could only cross sixth behind Piastri to complete a poor day for Ferrari. Despite his crash, Leclerc was able to remove himself from his stricken machine, but he was seen sitting on the grass in apparent pain. Russell held his nerve at the restart following a 30-minute red-flag period after Leclerc's crash to keep clear of Pierre Gasly with Antonelli making up six places from 12th. Russell soon had Verstappen for company and the Red Bull man streaked past his English rival for the lead on the 12th lap and by the start of the next lap, Antonelli had muscled his way up to third. A boost came for Russell two laps later when he snatched the lead back from Verstappen. But Antonelli breezed past the Red Bull driver on the next lap and was in second and on lap 18, the Italian led the race after seeing off Russell on the long run down to the Variante del Rettifilo. Over the next four laps, Antonelli and Russell traded positions four times for the lead before Russell got ahead of his team-mate on lap 23. Antonelli was called in by Mercedes for a pit-stop and was 14 seconds behind when he left the pits. With 10 laps to go Russell's advantage had been trimmed to just five seconds. The British driver was told to take "no risks" with his tyres with teammate in striking range. Antonelli thought he lost his chance when he ran through the sand trap with four laps to go but he got his man the next time around to secure a stunning fightback win. Australian Associated Press

items.article_search_text: Alpine's Pierre Gasly delivered one of the best, most surprisingly good qualifying performances this season. Pierre Gaslyyyyyyy (in Daniel Ricciardo and Yuki Tsunoda's voices)! Saturday's qualifying session at Monza delivered the goods, and Alpine's Pierre Gasly is right in the center of it. In contrast, two of the favorites, Ferrari and McLaren, underwhelmed at the Temple of Speed [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/why-monza-is-f1-s-temple-of-speed-and-the-circuit-that-made-history]. REDEMPTION FOR THE FRENCHMAN This week has been a rollercoaster of emotions for Alpine driver Pierre Gasly. Before the weekend, he received news that his penalties at Monaco [https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/f1-championship-standings-monaco-gp-123529877.html] were reinstated, stripping him of a podium finish. As a result, Alpine took a hit in the Teams' Standings, dropping to 54 points. That's a big hit in their midfield race against the Racing Bulls. But Gasly put his head down and went to work on Saturday. Alpine clearly got the setup on their car right, with both of their drivers advancing to Q3. Then, with George Russell setting the provisional fastest time, Gasly sped down the asphalt and snatched pole [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/pierre-gasly-stuns-monza-to-claim-historic-italian-grand-prix-pole-position] by a mere .060 advantage. This was Gasly's first pole position in Formula One, and it was a feat that he will never forget. PIASTRI'S PROMISING SATURDAY UNRAVELS Finally, it looked like Oscar Piastri was about to outperform McLaren teammate Lando Norris. Norris has won the last two races, adding more motivation for the Australian driver to do better this weekend. In the running for pole in Q3, Piastri would botch his final fast lap, locking up and exceeding track limits early in the lap. He had to settle for a third-place start, but not for long. Piastri incurred a three-place grid penalty for impeding Red Bull driver Liam Lawson in Q2. He will start sixth on Sunday, two spots ahead of Norris. SO MUCH FOR THE HOME TEAM'S UPGRADES Most of the people in the grandstand left dissatisfied, as Ferrari clearly lacked the pace to fight for pole position. Heading into this weekend, the home team stirred up hype with a newly upgraded power unit and a revised floor board, only for Charles Leclerc to qualify P4 and Lewis Hamilton P5. The Piastri penalty bumped both drivers to P3 and P4, but it was still a disappointing Saturday for the Prancing Horse. RED BULL DRIVER MIGHT MISS THIRD CONSECUTIVE RACE Due to a wrist injury, Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar is sitting out his second straight race weekend at Monza. Rumors have it that Hadjar will also miss the Spanish Grand Prix next week, as he's still recovering from his injury. Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said that it will be "difficult" for Hadjar to return to action at the Madring race, which is scheduled for September 11-13.

Stay up to date with all of the breaking sport, politics, entertainment, finance, weather and business headlines. Today's news, live updates & all the latest breaking stories from 7NEWS. McLaren’s Oscar Piastri qualified third at the ‘Temple of Speed’ but was then handed a three-place penalty at the Italian Grand Prix for impeding Red Bull’s Liam Lawson. It was a big blow for the Australian as Pierre Gasly delivered the shock of the season by taking the first pole position of his career for Sunday’s race. Piastri slowed to allow Lawson’s teammate Max Verstappen through but delayed the New Zealander — a Red Bull substitute — when he slotted in ahead of him at the first chicane during the closing stages of Q2. “Dude, what the f***,” Lawson could be heard saying immediately after the incident. After hearing from both drivers, Red Bull and McLaren team representatives, and reviewing the range of data available to them, the stewarding panel settled on a grid drop for the Australian. That meant Piastri — currently seventh in the standings — fell from third to sixth on the grid, promoting Ferrari pair Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton, as well as the Red Bull of Lawson’s team mate, Max. George Russell, widely expected to claim a much-needed pole in his world championship quest, had to settle for second on Saturday, pipped to top spot by Gasly by just 0.060 seconds. Speaking before the penalty was applied, Piastri said: “It was a tricky situation to manage. I was coming out of the pits and got told that Lawson and Verstappen were coming, but I kind of had to jump on the brakes pretty heavily to get out of Max’s way, and then I was just stuck in a very awkward spot with Liam.” Piastri added: “The speed difference coming out of the pits is so big here, so I don’t really know where he came from.” Gasly’s improbable triumph arrived a day on from his Alpine boss Flavio Briatore accusing an FIA judge of having a “working relationship” with McLaren after the British team’s appeal led to the Frenchman being stripped of his podium from June’s Monaco Grand Prix. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli took seventh but will start his home race from the back of the grid as he serves an engine penalty. World champion Lando Norris arrived in Italy with consecutive victories under his belt but looks almost certain to miss out on a hat-trick after he could manage only ninth. With Antonelli starting Sunday’s 53-lap race from the rear, Russell knew this event would hand him a golden chance to eat into his Mercedes teammate’s 59-point championship lead. But the Englishman will have to see off Gasly’s unexpected challenge to claim a full quota of points in what could prove a pivotal contest in the title race with 11 rounds still to go. Hamilton spoke about his dream of winning in Monza for a record sixth time and a first for Ferrari in the build-up to the Italian team’s home event. But the seven-time world champion endured a difficult afternoon. At one stage, Hamilton’s presence in Q3 appeared in grave danger after he could set only the 10th quickest time. However, his blushes were spared by just one- thousandth of a second. It was an unsatisfactory afternoon for Red Bull with Verstappen – who claimed his car was “broken” and “undriveable” – three-tenths off the pace. But there were no such concerns for Gasly as he flourished in his Alpine. “I have been waiting for that one,” yelled the Frenchman – whose sole victory of his Formula One life arrived in Monza six years ago – over the radio. Fernando Alonso qualified 21st, with only Aston Martin teammate Lance Stroll slower. Journalist from the 7NEWS.com.au team.

Oscar Piastri has been awarded a three-place grid penalty for impeding Liam Lawson during qualifying for the Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix. Piastri put early qualifying struggles aside to put his McLaren third on the grid for Sunday's race, but concern was raised in Q3 he could be in hot water with the stewards after an incident with Liam Lawson. Lawson, starting his final Q2 run, had ventured onto the track before the rest of the field with Max Verstappen to ensure he had a tow on his lap, vital on Monza's long straights, But the New Zealander's hopes were dashed as he approached Turn 1, entering the corner as Piastri joined the circuit, blocking Lawson's line and forcing him to slow down, Lawson was eliminated at the chequered flag. The stewards noted the incident before opening an investigation. Their decision was to penalise Piastri, stripping him of third place by imposing a three-place grid penalty. In their rationale, the stewards explained that Piastri stated he was not aware of Verstappen and Lawson's push laps, so took no avoiding action. Read full stewards decision bel ow "The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 81 (Oscar Piastri), the driver of Car 30 (Liam Lawson), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, timing, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence. "On leaving the pits, the driver of Car 81 was advised that “Verstappen, Lawson and Sainz just crossing, Sainz has pitted, Just Verstappen and Lawson, watch out for them as you join”. The driver of Car 81 stated that he was not alerted to the fact that VER and LAW were on push laps but realised as he was almost at turn 1 that VER was on a push lap. He slowed significantly and kept to the right to allow VER to pass but was unable to do anything to avoid impeding LAW who was close behind. "The Stewards accept that with the information he had, and the situation he was placed in, the driver of Car 81 had, at this stage, no other options available and hence, inadvertently, and also unnecessarily, impeded Car 30. Therefore the standard penalty of a drop of 3 grid positions is imposed." READ MORE: Pierre Gasly takes shock pole position for F1 Italian GP
